data.name: Purva
data.gender_notes: Purva is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Purva means 'the first, foremost, ancient'. It is derived from the Sanskrit root 'pur', which means 'first' or 'foremost'. In Hindu mythology, Purva is the name of the wife of the god Brahma, and also of one of the 27 stars in the constellation of the Pleiades. The name Purva carries the meaning “First, Foremost, Ancient” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Purva usually hope their child will grow to embody first, foremost, ancient and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of the beginning, the start of a new cycle.
data.etymology: Purva belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “First, Foremost, Ancient.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Purva total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Purva holds immense significance in Indian culture, specifically in Hindu mythology, as the name of the first or foremost wife of the creator god, Lord Brahma. It is also the name of one of the 27 stars in the constellation of the Pleiades, which is revered in astronomy and astrology. In the Hindu scripture, Mahabharata, the character Abhimanyu is believed to have been born while the constellation of Purva or Hasta was ascending and hence he is considered a warrior of great importance. In addition, in Hindu rituals and ceremonies, the Purva Muhurat, consulted under the guidance of astrologers, is considered the most propitious time for commencing new ventures.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Purva represents the essence of primordial creation and the beginning of all things. It symbolizes the figure of Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge and wisdom, as she is the first goddess to be created in the universe. Saraswati is believed to have emerged from the divine voice of Lord Brahma and embodies the wisdom of the Vedas and the knowledge of all things. Furthermore, the name Purva is said to evoke feelings of purity, freshness, and new beginnings.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Purva in Sanskrit means 'early', 'former', or 'previous'. Spiritually, it symbolizes being rooted in the past, preserving ancient wisdom and traditions, and embracing the lessons learned from experiences.

vedic_reference.note: The name Purva is derived from the Sanskrit word 'purvā' meaning 'first, old, prime'. It is not directly mentioned in the Vedas but is used in various Hindu texts and rituals.

historical_references.reference: The Purva Mimamsa Sutras are one of the six major works of Jaimini, an ancient Indian philosopher and grammarian. It is a key text in Mimamsa, a philosophical system that focuses on interpreting the Vedic scriptures. The Purva Mimamsa Sutras were likely composed between the 3rd and 1st centuries BCE.

Purva Paksha, also known as the 'opposing party', is a term used in Hindu and Buddhist legal and philosophical debates. It refers to the party presenting the opposing view to the one being argued for. The term is mentioned in various Indian texts, including the Mahabharata, and it is believed to have originated around the 1st millennium CE.

Despite its historical roots, this name is gaining popularity in modern contexts. According to recent data from Pinterest, searches for the name "Purva" have increased by 50% in the past year. This trend can also be seen on Instagram, where the hashtag #Purva has over 10,000 posts. Additionally, the baby name website Babycenter lists "Purva" as a trending name for girls of Indian origin.
